summary:
The SDBASE engine uses only the standard library, but it depends hard on Linux in five places:
- 10 modules import fcntl at module top. `sdbase/__init__.py` imports storage, so `import sdbase` itself fails on Windows.
- 7 helpers fsync directories through `os.open(dir)`. That raises PermissionError on Windows, and in `storage._atomic_json` it happens after the atomic replace has already succeeded.
- `backup._publish_absent` calls renameat2 through `ctypes.CDLL(None)`, which raises TypeError on Windows.
- WAL and replication publish files via `os.link(follow_symlinks=False)`.
- store_health, capacity_monitor and disk_index call `os.statvfs` and `os.pread`, which do not exist on Windows (AttributeError).

The durability design also relies on POSIX semantics Windows lacks. Renaming over a file another handle has open fails with WinError 5 or 32, even when the reader allowed FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Open or mmapped files cannot be deleted or removed by rmtree. Symlink checks ignore junctions, and `os.walk` descends into them. Every one of these was measured on the target machine (Windows 11 build 26300, official CPython 3.13.16 embeddable) rather than assumed.

The recommended design is one dependency-free shim, `sdbase/_platform.py`. A reference implementation was validated on the host and is included in the spec. Its POSIX branches are byte-identical to today's calls. Its Windows branches provide:
- LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx flock emulation at a high offset (OffsetHigh 0x7FFFFFFF, length 1), shared with C and the tools. Locks are mandatory on Windows, so locking byte 0 would block reads.
- Atomic replace with POSIX semantics via `SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx)`, a MoveFileExW fallback, and bounded retry.
- No-replace publish via plain rename.
- A best-effort directory FlushFileBuffers (works, about 0.2 ms).
- Binary, non-inheritable, share-delete opens via CreateFileW, with a race-free O_NOFOLLOW emulation.
- `pread` via ReadFile, disk space via GetDiskFreeSpaceExW, junction-aware link checks, one strict manifest-path parser for both OSes, and a robust rmtree.
- Private directories created and checked by ACL instead of mode bits. When the process is elevated, Python 3.13's `mkdir(0o700)` makes the Administrators group the directory's owner, and the same user running un-elevated later cannot open it.

Changes stay inside each module's existing helper names, because tools and acceptance tests import and monkeypatch them. There is only one real text-mode corruption path: `endpoint_journal` writes with raw `os.write`, which produces CRLF lines. `os.fdopen` already forces binary mode elsewhere; O_BINARY is still added everywhere.

The database format is byte-portable. Windows Python verified all 3,417 frames of the real 707 MB Linux journal with zero checksum failures, and engine metadata stores only relative POSIX paths. However, `desktop_mutations` receipts and their `_audit` copies contain absolute `/home/...` managed_path and backup values, which the desktop layer must stop replaying.

The main operational risks:
- Defender, the Search indexer and OneDrive holding handles on data files.
- FFmpeg or the HTTP media stream holding media objects open, which blocks repair and deletion.
- Long paths are disabled on this machine, so the 260-character limit applies.
- Durability ordering relies on NTFS behaviour.
- The engine's HTTP listeners can silently double-bind the same port through SO_REUSEADDR.
key_decisions: One dependency-free shim, `database/SDBASE/src/sdbase/_platform.py`, shared by all engine modules. The tools load the same file by path, so the constants are defined once. Its POSIX branches reproduce today's calls exactly.

Keep every existing private helper name and call site (`storage._atomic_json`, `backup._fsync_dir`/`_fsync_tree`/`_open_regular`/`_safe_source`/`_publish_absent`/`_copy_file`/`_inventory`, `endpoint_journal._fsync_directory`, `media._stage_object`, `replication._copy_file`) and change only their bodies. Tools and acceptance tests import these names and monkeypatch them.

Emulate flock with LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx on a fixed region: OVERLAPPED.Offset=0, OffsetHigh=0x7FFFFFFF, length 1. Contention with LOCK_NB raises BlockingIOError(EAGAIN). LOCK_UN ignores ERROR_NOT_LOCKED (158). Always unlock explicitly before closing. Same-handle re-locking and SH/EX conversion are unsupported, and no engine call site needs them.

Replace on Windows uses `SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx)` with REPLACE_IF_EXISTS and POSIX_SEMANTICS, which was verified to work over readers that allow FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Fall back to `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH)` on FAT, exFAT and some SMB volumes. Retry winerror 5/32/33/1224 with exponential backoff for up to 5 s (`SDBASE_FS_RETRY_SECONDS`).

All engine `os.open` calls go through the shim. On Windows that means CreateFileW with share READ|WRITE|DELETE, binary, non-inheritable, plus a race-free O_NOFOLLOW emulation (FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and a name-surrogate tag check that raises ELOOP). This also fixes the endpoint_journal CRLF corruption.

No-replace publishing on Windows: directories use `os.rename` (MoveFileExW without the replace flag), and files use rename instead of a hard link, which also works on exFAT. FileExistsError on conflict is kept, and callers' `finally: unlink` stays valid.

Directory fsync on Windows is a best-effort FlushFileBuffers on a GENERIC_WRITE + BACKUP_SEMANTICS handle (verified, about 0.2 ms). It never fails except for a missing directory, and `SDBASE_DIR_FSYNC=0` turns it into a no-op. Durability ordering rests on NTFS writing its metadata log in order, which the spec argues in §7.
Treat junctions and mount points (any reparse point with the name-surrogate bit) as symlinks everywhere via `is_link_like` / `entry_is_link_like`. Filter `os.walk` subdirectories the same way.

Parse manifest-relative paths with one parser on both OSes: '/' separators only; reject backslash, ':', NUL, '.', '..', empty components, trailing dot or space, and reserved device names. Stored paths stay POSIX f-strings.

Privacy uses ACLs instead of mode bits. `private_dir_ok` inspects the DACL. `mkdir_private` and `mkdtemp_private` create a protected DACL for SYSTEM, Administrators and the current user's SID, with that user as owner. This avoids Python 3.13's OWNER RIGHTS mode-0700 behaviour, which makes Administrators the owner when the process is elevated.
Use GetDiskFreeSpaceExW's available-to-caller value (the equivalent of statvfs `f_bavail`) instead of `shutil.disk_usage().free`. Implement `pread` with ReadFile and an OVERLAPPED offset.
Never keep persistent journal or lock handles. Per-operation open/close stays, so that a replace of the journal cannot strand a writer on the old, unlinked file.

No database conversion step: the format is byte-portable. Leave the `_audit` history untouched. Absolute Linux paths stored in desktop receipts are fixed in the desktop layer by recomputing them at replay time, not by rewriting data.
Engine HTTP listeners on Windows set `allow_reuse_address=False` and SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, and always connect to 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost (localhost measured at about 2 s per connect).
risks: Defender, the Search indexer, OneDrive or backup agents holding handles on files cause sharing violations and slow commits. The 700 MB journal is opened and closed on every operation. Retries bound the failures, but an exclusive-lock writer can stall up to the retry budget. Keep `data\` out of OneDrive, mark it not-content-indexed, and recommend a Defender exclusion.

Media objects held open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE by FFmpeg in the C player, or by `http_server.py:490` while streaming, block the corrupt-object repair (media.py:185) and any deletion. These must surface as a MediaError after the retry window.

Mapped disk-index files cannot be deleted. `recover_disk_index_builds(cleanup=True)` and the replication cache sweep must report or defer files that are in use instead of raising. An exception in `service_actions` would kill the replication listener.
Without POSIX directory fsync, checkpoint durability relies on NTFS writing its metadata log in order. FAT32, exFAT and SMB data volumes give weaker guarantees and should be warned about or refused.

Python 3.13's `mkdir(0o700)`/`mkdtemp` behaviour under an elevated run creates directories owned by Administrators, which the same user cannot open later without elevation. Published `.wal`, backup and replica directories made that way would become inaccessible unless all creation goes through `mkdir_private`.

Long paths are disabled on this machine (`RtlAreLongPathsEnabled` is False). Deep project roots plus build and stage names can exceed 260 characters. `realpath` may return `\\?\` forms or UNC forms (mapped or subst drives), which the C side must accept.

Path identity between Python and C: `resolve()` may turn a mapped drive into a UNC path, and letter case can differ. The C containment check of managed_path against database_file (planner.c:309) must canonicalize the same way and compare case-insensitively.

LockFileEx is not re-entrant per handle: a second exclusive lock on the same handle fails with error 33. Any future code that re-locks or converts a lock on the same fd will behave differently than flock.
Extending symlink checks to junctions on ancestor directories turns a junction-relocated data folder into an 'unsafe path' error. This matches the Linux behaviour for symlinks but may surprise users.
Without signals, graceful stop depends on the service wrapper setting each loop's `threading.Event` (named event). Abrupt `TerminateProcess` remains crash-safe.

Turkish case folding: NTFS treats ı/I/i as one case class while Python's `str.lower` does not. Containment checks on user-chosen Turkish directory names could disagree with the file system in contrived cases.
CTest will likely run under MSYS2 Python 3.14 while the product ships the 3.13 embeddable. Behaviour can differ subtly, so run the engine tests under both interpreters.
cross_area_dependencies: C portability layer: identical lock region and flags (Offset=0, OffsetHigh=0x7FFFFFFF, length 1; exclusive = LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK; non-blocking = LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY) for gui.lock, the outbox .lock, server.lock and RadioS.sdb.lock. Python tests probe the C GUI's gui.lock (test_application_shutdown.py:29-39, test_reliability.py:313-317).

C portability layer: open media objects and DB sidecars with FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|DELETE, so engine replace and unlink are not blocked. FFmpeg's file: protocol does not do this; a custom AVIO may be needed.
C (planner.c:309, media/playout): canonical, case-insensitive containment check of managed_path under `<database_file>.objects\`. It must accept UNC and `\\?\` forms produced by Python's `resolve()`.

tools/ launcher and service helpers: load `sdbase/_platform.py` by file path. Replace fcntl, direct `os.O_NOFOLLOW`/`os.O_NONBLOCK`, `st_uid != os.getuid()` (radios_reliability.py:371/385/390), `mode & 0o077` checks, `/proc`, and SIGTERM/SIGKILL with shim functions (`owner_ok`, `private_dir_ok`, `process_identity`, named stop events). Use `_platform.replace` for sidecar moves (radios_reliability.py:431). Never hold engine files open while renaming their parent directory.

Service wrapper (tools area): set the engine loops' stop events from a Windows named event or console handler. The affected loops are `run_online_maintenance`, `ops_scheduler.run_locked_loop`, `FailoverSupervisor.run`, `follow_forever`, and `serve_replication`'s `shutdown()`.

desktop_media area: replace `media._stage_object(store, Path('/proc/self/fd/N'))` (desktop_media.py:624) with `media._stage_object(store, fd)`. Replace the dir_fd/O_DIRECTORY/O_NONBLOCK opens (desktop_media.py:540-542) with `_platform.open_regular`. Stop persisting and replaying absolute managed_path/backup values in desktop_mutations receipts; recompute them at read time.

HTTP area (api_server.py, http_server.py): `BoundedHTTPServer` needs SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE and `allow_reuse_address=False` on Windows (failover_server and replication_stream depend on it). Stream media through a share-delete fd from `_platform.open_regular`.

Build/test area: the PYTHONPATH separator must be an escaped `\;` (CMakeLists.txt:916 and :1092). Fix `WORKING_DIRECTORY /tmp` (CMakeLists.txt:264). Port the tests that depend on fcntl, SIGKILL, /proc or symlink creation, register the new `_platform` tests, and run the engine tests under both the 3.13 embeddable and MSYS2 Python.

Packaging/installer: put the data root outside OneDrive, mark it NOT_CONTENT_INDEXED, recommend a Defender exclusion, enable LongPathsEnabled or keep the path budget, add `.gitattributes` `data/** -text`, and warn about FAT/exFAT/SMB data volumes.
platform_api_needs: Python `sdbase._platform.flock(fd_or_file, operation: int) -> None`: fcntl-compatible, with LOCK_SH=1, LOCK_EX=2, LOCK_NB=4, LOCK_UN=8. On Windows it calls LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx on `msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)` at OVERLAPPED Offset=0, OffsetHigh=0x7FFFFFFF, length 1. Contention with LOCK_NB (error 33 or 997) raises `BlockingIOError(EAGAIN)`. LOCK_UN on an unlocked handle is a no-op (ERROR_NOT_LOCKED ignored). It is not re-entrant per handle and does not convert SH/EX.

Python `lock(fd, *, exclusive: bool, timeout: float | None = None, poll: float = 0.01) -> None`: blocking when timeout is None, otherwise polls with LOCK_NB and raises TimeoutError on expiry. Also `unlock_and_close(fd: int) -> None`, and the context manager `locked_file(path, *, exclusive, timeout=None, create=False, write=False, mode=0o600)` that yields an fd.

Python `os_open(path, flags: int, mode: int = 0o777, *, nofollow: bool = False) -> int`. POSIX: `os.open(path, flags|O_CLOEXEC|(O_NOFOLLOW if nofollow), mode)`. Windows: CreateFileW with share READ|WRITE|DELETE, then `msvcrt.open_osfhandle`, giving a binary, non-inheritable fd. Dispositions map from O_CREAT/O_EXCL/O_TRUNC and the O_APPEND flag is passed through. With nofollow, a symlink or junction raises `OSError(errno.ELOOP)` with no race window. Errors map through winerror to FileNotFoundError, PermissionError or FileExistsError.
Python `open_flags(base: int, *, nofollow: bool = False) -> int` returns `base | O_BINARY | O_NOINHERIT | O_CLOEXEC | (O_NOFOLLOW if nofollow)`; constants that do not exist are 0.

Python `open_regular(path, *, write=False, create=False, mode=0o600, nofollow=True) -> int` opens without following links and checks `S_ISREG(fstat)`, raising `OSError(EINVAL)` otherwise. Also `read_bytes_shared(path, *, limit=None) -> bytes`, a share-delete read that never blocks a concurrent replace.

Python `fsync_dir(path) -> bool`. POSIX: open the directory with `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY` and fsync it. Windows: best-effort FlushFileBuffers on a CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS) handle; returns False on access-denied or unsupported, raises FileNotFoundError if the directory is missing; `SDBASE_DIR_FSYNC=0` makes it a no-op. Also `fsync_tree(root) -> None`, which walks bottom-up.

Python `replace(src, dst, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> None`. POSIX: `os.replace`. Windows: SetFileInformationByHandle(FileRenameInfoEx, REPLACE_IF_EXISTS|POSIX_SEMANTICS) on a DELETE handle, falling back to MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH) when the volume rejects it (winerror 1/50/87). Retries winerror 5/32/33/1224 with exponential backoff up to `SDBASE_FS_RETRY_SECONDS` (default 5 s), then re-raises the last error.

Python `publish_dir_noreplace(src, dst, *, timeout=None) -> None`. POSIX: renameat2(AT_FDCWD, src, AT_FDCWD, dst, RENAME_NOREPLACE) via ctypes; OSError(ENOSYS) if renameat2 is missing. Windows: `os.rename` (MoveFileExW without flags, which never replaces) with retry on 5/32. Raises FileExistsError if dst exists.

Python `link_noreplace(src, dst, *, timeout=None) -> None`. POSIX: `os.link(src, dst, follow_symlinks=False)`. Windows: `os.rename` with retry, which consumes src. Raises FileExistsError if dst exists.

Python `rmtree(path, *, timeout=None, ignore_errors=False) -> bool`. Windows: `shutil.rmtree` with an onexc handler that clears FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY and retries winerror 5/32 until the deadline; returns False when ignore_errors is set and removal failed.
Python `pread(fd, length, offset) -> bytes`. POSIX: `os.pread`. Windows: ReadFile with an OVERLAPPED offset on the OS handle; returns b'' at end of file.

Python `disk_usage(path) -> tuple[int, int]` returning (total_bytes, bytes_available_to_caller). POSIX: statvfs `f_blocks*f_frsize`, `f_bavail*f_frsize`. Windows: GetDiskFreeSpaceExW (total, FreeBytesAvailableToCaller).

Python `is_link_like(path) -> bool` (S_ISLNK, or a reparse point with the name-surrogate bit 0x20000000: symlink, junction or mount point; never raises) and `entry_is_link_like(entry: os.DirEntry) -> bool`.

Python `safe_relative_parts(relative: str) -> tuple[str, ...]`: strict manifest-path parser, identical on both OSes. Separators are '/' only. Raises ValueError for empty input, NUL, backslash, ':', absolute paths, '', '.' or '..' components, a trailing dot or space, and (on Windows) reserved device names. Also `valid_new_name(name: str) -> bool` for names of new target directories.

Python `mkdir_private(path, *, exist_ok=False) -> None` (POSIX: `mkdir(0o700)`; Windows: CreateDirectoryW with SDDL `O:<user>D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;FA;;;<user SID>)`), `mkdtemp_private(prefix='tmp', suffix='', dir=None) -> str`, and the context manager `temporary_directory(prefix, suffix, dir)`, whose cleanup on Windows retries and never masks the body's exception.

Python `private_dir_ok(path) -> bool`. POSIX: `S_ISDIR and not mode & 0o077`. Windows: the owner must be the user, SYSTEM or Administrators; a NULL DACL fails; every effective ACCESS_ALLOWED ACE may grant access only to the user, SYSTEM, Administrators, CREATOR OWNER, TrustedInstaller, or OWNER RIGHTS when the owner is allowed. Also `current_user_sid() -> str` and `long_paths_enabled() -> bool` (RtlAreLongPathsEnabled).

C `include/radios/platform.h`: `RADIOS_LOCK_OFFSET_LOW 0x00000000u`, `RADIOS_LOCK_OFFSET_HIGH 0x7FFFFFFFu`, `RADIOS_LOCK_LENGTH 1u`, plus `gboolean radios_file_lock(int fd, gboolean exclusive, gboolean nonblocking, GError **error)` and `void radios_file_unlock(int fd)`, implemented with LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx on exactly that region. Contention reports a would-block error, and unlocking an unlocked region is ignored. This lets C and Python locks interoperate on the same lock files.

C `int radios_open_shared(const char *utf8_path, int flags, int mode)`: binary, non-inheritable CRT fd opened via CreateFileW with FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE|FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Used for media objects and DB sidecars read by the C app, so engine replace and unlink are not blocked.

Tools-shim additions (owned by the tools area, same module): `process_identity(pid) -> tuple[int, int] | None` (pid plus creation FILETIME via OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and GetProcessTimes); `owner_ok(path) -> bool` (owner SID equals the current user SID); `named_stop_event(name) -> threading.Event` and `signal_stop(name) -> bool` using CreateEventW/OpenEventW/SetEvent on `Local\RadioS-<sha256(root)[:16]>-<service>-stop`.
